clips.caption:
Nobody starts out this way.

Somewhere back in childhood, something happened enough times that it left a mark - not just a memory, but actual damage to the limbic system. A different wiring.

What grows out of that wiring is a person who feels completely empty inside, no matter what they build or achieve. So they go looking outside themselves for something to fill it - your attention, your approval, your energy.

The emptiness was always theirs. You just happened to be standing where they came looking for it.

#subconscious #innerwork #awakening #selfawareness #emotionalhealing #kevintrudeau

This isn't a personality flaw. It's biology.

Every time a child is thrown into fight or flight - and it happens on a loop, not once - cortisol floods the brain. Do that long enough and the limbic system, the emotional core, stops developing normally. It stays hypersensitive for life.

So the adult version of that brain reads an eye roll, a tone of voice, as a threat to survival. The logical part shuts off completely. What's left is raw, unfiltered emotion.

Understanding where it came from won't fix the relationship. But it tells you exactly why reasoning with it never worked.

You didn't just bring yourself into this relationship.

You brought who you really are. And you brought the version of you still carrying whatever wasn't healed from childhood - the one still looking to be loved in a way it never quite was. Your partner brought the same two.

Four people in the room, and most of the talking gets done by the two nobody introduced. That's why the same fight keeps happening in a different outfit, with a different person saying it.

Heal what you're carrying, or it keeps choosing for you.

A reporter once asked Deepak Chopra about the documentary his own son made, tearing him apart on camera.

Deepak's answer: "He didn't do a documentary about me. He did a documentary about himself."

What you see in someone else is a mirror, not a window. The people constantly pointing out every narcissist, every toxic ex, every controlling partner - three fingers are pointing back at them while the one points out.

You don't see the world as it is. You see the world as you are.

They don't pick you because you're nothing. They pick you because you're too much.

A narcissist doesn't attach to someone low-value - there's no supply in that, nothing worth draining. They attach to the person with real warmth, real competence, real light, and then spend the relationship trying to dim it.

If they're working that hard to devalue you, read it correctly: it's because there was something there worth devaluing in the first place.

The scary ones aren't the obvious ones.

A covert narcissist reads to the rest of the world as kind, sweet, humble - even a little bit of a victim. That's exactly what makes them impossible to call out: who's going to believe you over someone that nice?

She found out the way most people do - too late, in the middle of a business partnership, reading a book about it on a plane while her husband shushed her gasping. "Oh my God, this is exactly what this person is."

The kindness isn't fake. It's just not the whole picture.
